haiku-low.q1: The 02:00 UTC scheduler starts it. It extracts replica orders with updated_at between watermark minus 2 hours and the replica clock when the snapshot opens.
haiku-low.q2: Bulk imports hold transactions open up to 90 minutes, and updated_at is stamped at write time, not commit, so rows can show up on the replica up to 90 minutes late.
haiku-low.q3: The app bumps updated_at on every write, so the edited row comes back in the next night's extract, and the merge replaces the older copy.
haiku-low.q4: The app sets deleted_at, which flows through the merge and sets is_deleted = true on the warehouse row. Nothing is ever deleted from fact_orders.
haiku-low.q5: That attempt's transaction never commits, so the target and watermark stay untouched. The next try clears staging and reruns, up to 3 tries 15 minutes apart, then on-call is paged.
haiku-low.q6: Dashboards show the last committed data. The 06:00 check posts a staleness alert to #data-alerts when etl_runs has no successful try for tonight.
haiku-low.q7: The Sunday recon job reloads mismatched days, but only for orders created in the last 30 days and only if Sunday's nightly actually succeeded.
haiku-low.q8: The merge keys on order_id and overwrites an existing row only when the staged updated_at is strictly newer than the target's. Otherwise the row is skipped.
haiku-low.q9: In etl_watermark, a single warehouse row. It gets the upper bound (replica clock when the snapshot opened), committed in the same transaction as the merge and success status.
haiku-low.q10: The merge, watermark write and run success status commit in one transaction, and dashboards read only fact_orders, so they see the whole night or none of it.
haiku-low.q11: Staging is cleared at the start of every try, so the failed attempt's staged data is discarded. The retry rereads the same checkpoint with a fresh upper bound, lower bound watermark minus 2 hours.
haiku-low.q12: Recon re-reads all orders created that day from the replica, stages them and applies them through the same merge in its own transaction. It never moves the high-water mark.

sonnet.q1: The scheduler kicks it off at 02:00 UTC. It reads the read replica only and extracts orders whose updated_at is after the lower bound (watermark minus 2h) and up to the upper bound (replica clock when the snapshot opens).
sonnet.q2: Bulk imports in the app hold transactions open for up to 90 minutes, and updated_at is stamped when the row is written, not at commit. So the rows can show up on the replica up to 90 minutes late.
sonnet.q3: The app bumps updated_at on every write, so the row comes back in the next night's extract. The merge overwrites the warehouse row because the staged updated_at is strictly newer.
sonnet.q4: The app sets deleted_at (a soft delete, which is a write) and never hard-deletes. The change comes through the normal extract and merge, and the warehouse row gets is_deleted = true. Nothing is ever deleted from fact_orders.
sonnet.q5: The transaction never commits, so the target and the HWM are untouched. The run retries after 15 minutes, with at most 3 tries per night. If the 3rd try fails, on-call is paged.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards refresh at 06:00 UTC regardless and show the last committed data. The 06:00 check finds no successful etl_runs try for tonight and posts a staleness alert to #data-alerts. (On-call is also paged if all 3 tries failed.)
sonnet.q7: The Sunday recon job. It compares each day of the last 30 days by order creation day (row count plus checksum over order_id + updated_at) between the replica and the warehouse. For a mismatched day it re-pulls that day's orders and merges them. It only runs if that Sunday's nightly succeeded.
sonnet.q8: The merge is keyed on order_id. It inserts new ids. For an existing id it overwrites only when the staged updated_at is strictly newer than the target's, otherwise it skips the row.
sonnet.q9: It is stored in the warehouse, in etl_watermark (a single row). The value written is the upper bound, which is the replica's clock when the snapshot opened. It is written inside the same transaction as the merge and the run's success status, at commit.
sonnet.q10: The merge, the HWM write and the run success status happen in one transaction. Dashboards read only fact_orders, never the landing table, so they see either the whole night or none of it.
sonnet.q11: Every try starts by clearing stg, so the failed attempt's staged data is discarded. The retry reads the same checkpoint, so the lower bound is the same (watermark minus 2h), and it takes a fresh upper bound.
sonnet.q12: For each mismatched day, it re-reads every order created that day from the replica into stg_orders, which is cleared first. It pushes them through the same merge as the nightly, in its own transaction. It does not move the checkpoint (HWM).
